name: Data fragmentation

subjectOf.text: Cloud computing increased connectivity but simultaneously produced monolithic, siloed applications built for a single business, department, or role, and that fragmentation of data and content now impairs collaboration as well as the search, organization, and discovery of content.
subjectOf.abstract: Cloud computing has significantly increased connectivity in society and business but at the same time contributed to the creation of monolithic applications that solve a very specific problem for a specific business / department / role.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859

subjectOf.text: Access to structured labeled data determines which industries can capitalize on AI first: finance and healthcare hold a head start, while transportation and customer service face hurdles from privacy concerns, data fragmentation, and extensive labeling requirements.
subjectOf.abstract: Industries that can access large volumes of structured and labeled data, such as finance and healthcare, may have a head start in leveraging AI. On the other hand, industries like transportation and customer service may face hurdles in obtaining quality data
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Learning - Decentralized Governance to Optimize Human Output Datasets for AI Learning (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4755632
scope_conditions: applies to industries seeking to realize AI driven market potential
